title: Patagonian Landscape Post-Processing: History-Brush Workflow, Color Grading, and Panorama Stitching

locations.name: Fitz Roy (Cerro Fitz Roy)
locations.basis: Explicit mention of Fitzroy in transcript (multiple timestamps)

locations.name: Cerro Torre
locations.basis: Explicit mention alongside Guanaco in transcript

summary: This video presents an in-depth, Photoshop-centric workflow for turning raw landscape and drone imagery into richly rendered panoramas with strong depth and directional light. Through non-destructive techniques, the presenter demonstrates a history-state workflow (paint-adjustments on select states), zone-by-zone tonal shaping (shadows, blacks, whites, exposure), and meticulous edge work to separate layers. The session also covers panorama assembly with PT GUI, rectilinear projection for a natural wide view, and color-grade strategies (blue-gold filtration, 50/150 color adjustments, selective blues/greens) to enhance fall color and sky. Throughout, the emphasis is on cropping strategy (rule of six), directional lighting, and iterative back-and-forth refinement to achieve depth, mood, and cohesion across closely linked composition elements like foreground and distant peaks.
topics: history brush technique and painting highlights
camera raw tonal adjustments (shadows, blacks, whites, exposure)
dehaze for atmosphere and beam creation
panorama stitching workflow (PT GUI, rectilinear projection)
color grading using selective color and 50-150 color wheel
sky and foreground color balance (greens, reds, blues)
shadow dodge and highlight dodge techniques
drone imagery workflow and multi-shot stitching
final finishing touches: vignette, contrast, warmth
edge cleanup and avoiding halo artifacts

sections.title: Scene assessment and crop planning
concepts: crop off low-value edges to strengthen the frame
sections.description: The presenter surveys the frame, noting strong fall color layers and a less engaging foreground/sky split. He introduces cropping as a tool to remove distractions (edge clutter and the least compelling 1/6) and to set up a path for connecting disparate tonal regions.

sections.title: Global tonal balance and RAW prep (initial pass)
sections.description: An early RAW-based pass aims to reduce overall contrast to uncover more detail in shadows and to enable more control over light direction in later steps. Clarity, whites, warmth, and exposure are introduced as preliminary levers before localized adjustments.

sections.title: History-Brush based local adjustments (RAW)
concepts: preserving foreground/sky while enhancing middle tones
sections.description: The workflow treats history states like non-destructive layers. The presenter creates a targeted adjustment in RAW, then uses the history brush to paint that state into specific regions, preserving prior edits and enabling iterative remixing.

sections.title: Directional light shaping and zone-by-zone edits
concepts: creating directional light via selective painting
sections.description: The frame is flattened zone-by-zone, then directional light is painted from the side to separate foreground, middle ground, and distant elements. De-haze is introduced carefully to avoid over-processing while enhancing depth.

sections.title: Edge separation and complex masking (hard/soft brush)
concepts: preventing hard lines in complex compositions
sections.description: When certain mountain edges cannot be easily masked, the artist traces with a hard-edge brush and then blends with soft brushes. The goal is to create a believable separation between layers and to hide disruptive seams.

sections.title: Iterative refinement and field context (drone shots)
concepts: prepping for panoramas and future edits
sections.description: The speaker discusses the broader field context (drone captures and different scouting angles) and emphasizes iterative adjustment, confirmation of good light, and selecting frames suitable for later stitching or compositing.

sections.title: Panorama workflow with PT GUI and Photoshop prep
concepts: camera raw post-process steps after stitching
sections.description: The process shifts toward constructing panoramas. The presenter uses PT GUI to stitch multiple drone shots with rectilinear projection to emulate a wide-angle capture, then explores post-process workflow in Photoshop after exporting a TIFF from PT GUI.

sections.title: Fall color color-grading and sky handling
sections.description: Color grading focuses on enhancing fall colors and sky interplay. Tools demonstrated include the 50/150 color-wheel method, selective color adjustments, and a blue-gold calibration to influence sky tones before local painting and masking.

sections.title: Atmosphere, beams, and final touches
sections.description: The final segment emphasizes atmospheric depth via light haze, beam creation, and selective dodging/burning. The presenter cautions about overdoing atmospheric effects, demonstrates a save-versus-overwrite strategy (save multiple versions), and discusses decisions about color balance, contrast, and edge darkening to guide the viewer’s eye through the frame.

featured_techniques.technique: History brush workflow in Photoshop to non-destructively apply and remix adjustments across multiple history states
Panorama stitching with PT GUI using rectilinear projection to simulate 9mm-wide field of view
Blue-gold filter and selective color adjustments for sky and fall foliage
50-150 color wheel method for color separation (greens vs. reds) in fall scenery
Hard-edge masking and tracing around hard-to-select edges to separate layers
Directional lighting via staged painting of whites/shadows to emphasize light direction
